easy.prompt: In the attention mechanism, what does the softmax over keys produce?

choices.label: A
choices.body: The raw dot products without normalization

choices.label: B
choices.body: A probability distribution over positions to weight values.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A fixed one-hot vector over the sequence

choices.label: D
choices.body: The gradient of the loss with respect to queries

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Attention weights αᵢ = softmax(score(q, kᵢ)); they sum to 1 and select how much of each value to blend.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Dot products are scores; softmax turns them into weights.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Softmax yields a full distribution, not a single hard index (unless degenerate).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Softmax is part of the forward pass, not backprop by definition here.

easy.prompt: Scaled dot-product attention divides dot products by √d_k primarily to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Keep softmax inputs in a moderate range so gradients do not vanish.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Make attention weights exactly uniform

choices.label: C
choices.body: Eliminate the need for positional encoding

choices.label: D
choices.body: Convert dot products into probabilities directly

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Large d_k makes dot-product magnitudes large; scaling prevents extremely peaked softmax and tiny gradients.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Scaling stabilizes variance; it does not force uniform weights.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Positional encoding addresses order; scaling addresses magnitude.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Softmax, not scaling alone, produces probabilities.

easy.prompt: The output of a single attention head is best described as…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A weighted sum of value vectors using attention weights on keys.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The maximum value vector in the sequence

choices.label: C
choices.body: The average of all keys without weighting

choices.label: D
choices.body: The element-wise product of query and key only

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: output = Σᵢ αᵢ vᵢ where αᵢ come from comparing the query to each key.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Attention blends values; argmax would be hard selection.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Keys set weights; values are what get summed.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Dot products score compatibility; values are aggregated, not just multiplied.

easy.prompt: In self-attention, queries, keys, and values are derived from…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A separate encoder-only memory bank

choices.label: B
choices.body: Random noise vectors sampled each step

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only the final token embedding

choices.label: D
choices.body: The same input sequence (via learned linear projections).

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Self-attention relates every position to every other position in one sequence: Q, K, V all come from X.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That describes cross-attention to another sequence.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Q, K, V are deterministic functions of embeddings.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: All positions participate, not just the last token.

easy.prompt: Self-attention lets each token directly attend to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Any other token in the same sequence.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Only tokens in a different batch element

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only padding tokens exclusively

choices.label: D
choices.body: Only its immediate left neighbor

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: All-pairs interactions build long-range dependencies in one layer (subject to masking in decoders).

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Attention is within one sequence instance.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Models mask padding out, not attend only to it.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That is local recurrence; self-attention is all-to-all.

easy.prompt: Compared with a single RNN layer over length n, vanilla self-attention's time complexity is often cited as…

choices.label: A
choices.body: O(1) regardless of sequence length

choices.label: B
choices.body: O(n) because it runs in one parallel pass

choices.label: C
choices.body: O(n³) due to three matmuls

choices.label: D
choices.body: O(n²) in sequence length for the attention matrix.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Computing all pairwise scores costs O(n²); parallel depth is O(1) per layer vs O(n) for RNNs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Longer sequences still increase attention cost.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Parallelism is good, but pairwise scores still scale quadratically.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: QKV projections are O(n); the bottleneck is n×n attention.

easy.prompt: Transformers have no built-in notion of token order, so positional encodings are added to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Reduce the vocabulary size

choices.label: B
choices.body: Inject information about each token's position in the sequence.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Normalize gradients across layers

choices.label: D
choices.body: Replace the embedding layer entirely

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Attention is permutation-invariant on embeddings alone; position tags break symmetry.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Vocabulary is unrelated to sequence order.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That is layer norm's role, not positional encoding.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Positions augment token embeddings, not replace them.

easy.prompt: Sinusoidal positional encodings in the original Transformer use…

choices.label: A
choices.body: One-hot vectors of length equal to vocabulary

choices.label: B
choices.body: Random Gaussian noise added once per epoch

choices.label: C
choices.body: Fixed sine and cosine waves at different frequencies per dimension.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Learned integer indices only at training time

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d}); cos on even/odd pairs gives smooth relative structure.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Position is not the same as token identity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Sinusoidal PE is fixed, not resampled noise.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Sinusoidal encodings are deterministic functions of position.

easy.prompt: In a Transformer for machine translation, the encoder typically…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Generates target tokens one at a time autoregressively

choices.label: B
choices.body: Stores only the final hidden state as a single vector

choices.label: C
choices.body: Applies causal masking to every position

choices.label: D
choices.body: Maps the source sentence to a stack of contextual representations.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: The encoder processes the full source with bidirectional (unmasked) self-attention.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Autoregressive generation is the decoder's job.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: All source positions remain available via representations.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Causal masking is used in the decoder, not the encoder stack.

easy.prompt: Decoder cross-attention lets each target position attend to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Only its own embedding without context

choices.label: B
choices.body: Encoder outputs (memory) while also using masked self-attention on prior targets.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Future target tokens not yet generated

choices.label: D
choices.body: Random keys from an unrelated batch

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Cross-attention queries come from the decoder state; keys and values come from encoder outputs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Cross-attention explicitly pulls source information.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Causal self-attention blocks future targets; cross-attn reads source.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Memory is aligned to the paired source sentence.

easy.prompt: Teacher forcing during Transformer training means…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Attention weights are frozen after epoch one

choices.label: B
choices.body: The teacher model has fewer layers than the student

choices.label: C
choices.body: The decoder input uses ground-truth previous tokens, not model predictions.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Gradients are disabled in the encoder

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Feeding correct prefixes speeds stable training; at inference the model feeds its own outputs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Weights continue to update throughout training.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Teacher forcing refers to inputs, not model distillation here.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Both stacks are typically trained jointly.

easy.prompt: Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel and then…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Concatenates head outputs and projects them with a linear layer.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Applies softmax across heads instead of positions

choices.label: C
choices.body: Discards all but the first head at inference

choices.label: D
choices.body: Averages all heads into a single scalar

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Each head has its own Q, K, V projections; concat + W_O mixes subspaces.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Softmax is over sequence positions within each head.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: All heads contribute at train and test time.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Head outputs are vectors concatenated, not reduced to one scalar.

easy.prompt: Using multiple heads allows the model to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Capture different relationship types (syntax, coreference, etc.) in parallel.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Reduce sequence length by a factor of h

choices.label: C
choices.body: Eliminate the feed-forward sublayer

choices.label: D
choices.body: Remove the need for layer normalization

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Different heads can specialize in distinct attention patterns over the same tokens.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Head count does not shorten the sequence.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: FFN remains part of each Transformer block.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Layer norm is still used around sublayers.

easy.prompt: If model dimension is d_model and there are h heads, each head typically uses dimension…

choices.label: A
choices.body: d_k = d_v = d_model / h

choices.label: B
choices.body: 1 regardless of h

choices.label: C
choices.body: d_model × h

choices.label: D
choices.body: twice the vocabulary size

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Splitting d_model across h heads keeps total parameter footprint manageable.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Heads use substantial subspaces, not scalars only.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Per-head dimension shrinks as h grows, not multiplies d_model.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Head size is architectural, not tied to |V|.

easy.prompt: Large language models are typically trained with a…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Pairwise ranking loss on image patches

choices.label: B
choices.body: Causal (autoregressive) next-token prediction objective.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Purely masked bidirectional objective on full sentences only

choices.label: D
choices.body: Clustering loss over document embeddings

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Given prefix tokens, the model predicts the distribution of the next token (MLE / cross-entropy).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: LLMs are text models; that describes vision ranking.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: BERT-style MLM is different from standard GPT-style LLM training.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: LLM pretraining is generative token modeling, not k-means.

easy.prompt: At inference, autoregressive LLMs generate text by repeatedly…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Re-training all weights after each character

choices.label: B
choices.body: Sampling or selecting one token, appending it, and conditioning on the longer prefix.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Sorting the vocabulary alphabetically each step

choices.label: D
choices.body: Encoding the entire future paragraph in one forward pass

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Each step extends the context; total cost grows with output length unless cached.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Weights are fixed at inference; only activations update.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Decoding uses model logits, not lexical sorting.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Future tokens are not known; generation is sequential.

easy.prompt: Temperature in LLM sampling scales logits before softmax to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Cache key-value pairs from prior layers

choices.label: B
choices.body: Control randomness — higher temperature yields flatter, more diverse distributions.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Enforce grammatical POS tags

choices.label: D
choices.body: Increase model depth dynamically

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: T > 1 spreads probability mass; T → 0 approaches greedy argmax.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That is KV-cache optimization, not temperature.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Sampling temperature does not hard-constrain syntax.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Temperature affects sampling, not architecture depth.

easy.prompt: During autoregressive decoding, a KV cache stores…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The entire training dataset in RAM

choices.label: B
choices.body: Gradients from the backward pass of prior tokens

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only the softmax attention weights from step zero

choices.label: D
choices.body: Previously computed key and value projections for past tokens.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Keys and values for prefix tokens are reused instead of recomputed each new step.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Caches hold activations for the current sequence, not the corpus.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Inference often runs without storing training gradients.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Caches store K and V tensors per layer, not just weights.

easy.prompt: KV caching speeds up decoding because each new token…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Reduces model parameters by half

choices.label: B
choices.body: Only needs a forward pass for its query attending to cached K/V of the prefix.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Eliminates the vocabulary softmax

choices.label: D
choices.body: Skips the attention mechanism entirely

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Work per step becomes roughly O(n) per layer on context length instead of recomputing O(n²) over the full prefix.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Parameter count is unchanged; compute is saved.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: The output projection and softmax still run each step.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Attention remains; prior K/V are reused.

easy.prompt: Memory used by a KV cache grows with…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Only the learning rate schedule

choices.label: B
choices.body: Context length, number of layers, batch size, and hidden dimension.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The number of training epochs completed

choices.label: D
choices.body: Whether layer norm uses bias terms

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Each layer stores K and V for all past positions — longer contexts mean larger caches.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Optimizer hyperparameters do not define cache size.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Cache size is a runtime inference concern, not epoch count.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Norm bias is tiny compared to per-token K/V storage.

medium.prompt: Bahdanau (additive) attention scores compatibility with…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A feed-forward network on concatenated or combined query and key features.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Only the L2 distance between value vectors

choices.label: C
choices.body: A fixed lookup table indexed by token ID

choices.label: D
choices.body: The determinant of the query-key outer product

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: score(q, k) = vᵀ tanh(W_q q + W_k k) generalizes dot-product when dimensions differ.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Values are aggregated after scoring; scoring uses q and k.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Scores are computed from representations, not static tables.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Attention scores are per-position scalars, not matrix determinants.

medium.prompt: When attention scores are very large before softmax, the distribution becomes…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Uniform with maximal gradient everywhere

choices.label: B
choices.body: Independent of the query vector

choices.label: C
choices.body: Always zero for every position

choices.label: D
choices.body: Nearly one-hot, with small gradients to non-argmax keys.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Peaked softmax saturates; scaling dot products mitigates this in Transformers.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Large logits yield peaked, not uniform, distributions.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Scores depend on q · k (or general score functions).
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Softmax always assigns positive mass summing to 1.

medium.prompt: In a Transformer encoder block, self-attention is followed by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A recurrent state passed to the next sentence only

choices.label: B
choices.body: A position-wise feed-forward network and residual connections with layer norm.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Deleting half the hidden dimensions permanently

choices.label: D
choices.body: A convolution with kernel size equal to vocabulary

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Pre-norm or post-norm variants wrap attention and FFN: Attn → FFN with residuals.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Blocks are depth-stacked; RNN hidden state is not the core pattern.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Dimension is preserved across the block (aside from internal FFN expansion).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: FFN is two linear layers with activation on each position.

medium.prompt: Causal (masked) self-attention in GPT-style models sets attention logits to −∞ for…

choices.label: A
choices.body: All padding tokens in both directions

choices.label: B
choices.body: Every pair of tokens in the encoder

choices.label: C
choices.body: Positions j > i so token i cannot attend to future tokens.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Only the first token in the sequence

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: An upper-triangular mask preserves autoregressive conditioning: predict next token from past.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Padding uses separate masks; causal mask is about temporal order.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Encoder self-attention is typically unmasked bidirectional.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Each position has its own allowed prefix set.

medium.prompt: Multi-layer self-attention stacks increase expressive power because…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Only the first layer may attend to all positions

choices.label: B
choices.body: Depth replaces the need for any parameters

choices.label: C
choices.body: Each layer removes positional information entirely

choices.label: D
choices.body: Later layers can build on increasingly mixed contextual representations.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Composition of attention + FFN lets higher layers model more abstract dependencies.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Every layer performs full (masked) attention over allowed positions.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: More layers add parameters and computation.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Positional signals propagate; depth refines context.

medium.prompt: Learned absolute positional embeddings differ from sinusoidal encodings in that they…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Are trainable vectors indexed by position, capped by a maximum length.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Encode only relative distance without any position index

choices.label: C
choices.body: Require no parameters and generalize beyond max length by formula

choices.label: D
choices.body: Replace token embeddings in the output softmax

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Learned PE is flexible but may not extrapolate well past trained max sequence length.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Absolute learned embeddings tie to index i.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That describes fixed sinusoidal encodings, not learned tables.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Positions are added to inputs, not the final logits layer.

medium.prompt: Relative positional bias (e.g., in T5 or some long-context models) modifies attention by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Removing keys from distant tokens entirely

choices.label: B
choices.body: Forcing all attention weights to be equal

choices.label: C
choices.body: Using only sinusoidal functions in the output layer

choices.label: D
choices.body: Adding a score based on distance i − j rather than only absolute position vectors.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Relative biases let the model generalize patterns like 'nearby vs far' across sequence lengths.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Bias shifts scores; it does not drop keys.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Bias changes relative preferences, not uniformity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Biases are often learned buckets or functions of distance.

medium.prompt: The original Transformer ties encoder and decoder with…

choices.label: A
choices.body: No attention between source and target

choices.label: B
choices.body: Shared embedding space and stacked layers where decoder cross-attends to encoder memory.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Identical weights for every encoder and decoder layer

choices.label: D
choices.body: A single RNN hidden state between both sides

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Embeddings may be shared; decoder layers consume encoder outputs via cross-attention.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Cross-attention is the bridge from source to target.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Layers are separate modules with different roles.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Transformers replace RNN state with attention memory.

medium.prompt: Beam search in Transformer decoding maintains…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The full attention matrix from training only

choices.label: B
choices.body: A single greedy path with no alternatives

choices.label: C
choices.body: All vocabulary words as equally likely each step

choices.label: D
choices.body: Multiple partial hypotheses ranked by cumulative log-probability.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Beam width b keeps top-b prefixes; expansion trades compute for better translations.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Beam search operates on decoding scores, not stored train matrices.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Beam search explicitly explores multiple prefixes.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Log-probs from the model rank continuations.

medium.prompt: Encoder-decoder models like T5 frame many NLP tasks as…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Purely contrastive image-caption ranking

choices.label: B
choices.body: Text-to-text generation with a unified span-corruption or instruction format.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Unsupervised k-means over byte n-grams only

choices.label: D
choices.body: Static template filling without neural parameters

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: T5 casts classification, translation, and QA as generating target text strings.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: T5 is text-to-text, not CLIP-style vision contrastive learning.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Training uses neural denoising / supervised text objectives.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: The model learns parameters end-to-end.

medium.prompt: With h heads and model dimension d_model, the concat of head outputs has dimension…

choices.label: A
choices.body: 2 × vocabulary size

choices.label: B
choices.body: h × (d_model / h) = d_model before the output projection.

choices.label: C
choices.body: h² × d_model

choices.label: D
choices.body: d_model / h²

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Each head outputs d_v = d_model/h; concatenating h heads restores width d_model.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Internal width is architectural, not 2|V|.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Concatenation is linear in h, not h squared times d_model.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Dimensions add across heads linearly, not divided twice.

medium.prompt: Grouped-query attention (GQA) reduces KV-cache memory by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Sharing one key-value head group among several query heads.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Removing queries entirely from inference

choices.label: C
choices.body: Using a vocabulary of size one

choices.label: D
choices.body: Storing only the softmax normalization constant

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Fewer distinct K/V projections are cached while queries remain numerous.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Queries are still computed each step; K/V are shared.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: GQA is a head grouping trick, not trivial vocab.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Caches hold K/V tensors, not just scalar norms.

medium.prompt: Attention dropout is typically applied to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The learning rate each optimizer step

choices.label: B
choices.body: Attention probability weights (or their dropped counterparts) during training.

choices.label: C
choices.body: All layer-normalization scale parameters

choices.label: D
choices.body: The final softmax over the vocabulary at decode time only

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Dropping attention edges regularizes which positions interact, similar to edge dropout.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Dropout is stochastic regularization, not LR scheduling.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Dropout targets activations/weights patterns, not γ in norm.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That is separate from attention-weight dropout inside the block.

medium.prompt: Instruction-tuned LLMs are usually built by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Training only the positional embedding table

choices.label: B
choices.body: Fine-tuning on prompt-response pairs (often after RLHF or preference optimization).

choices.label: C
choices.body: Freezing all layers and training solely the softmax bias

choices.label: D
choices.body: Removing the tokenizer and using raw bytes only

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Supervised fine-tuning (and optional RLHF/DPO) aligns behavior to human instructions.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Instruction tuning updates much of the network.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Far more than bias terms typically change.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Tokenization remains; tuning updates broader weights.

medium.prompt: Top-p (nucleus) sampling chooses the next token from…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A uniform random subset of size p tokens

choices.label: B
choices.body: The smallest set of highest-probability tokens whose cumulative mass exceeds p.

choices.label: C
choices.body: All tokens with probability below p only

choices.label: D
choices.body: Exactly the top 1 token always

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Nucleus sampling adapts breadth to model confidence, truncating the long tail.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: p is a cumulative probability threshold, not a count.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Nucleus keeps high-mass tokens, not the low tail.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That is greedy decoding; top-p keeps a variable-sized set.

medium.prompt: Context window limits in LLMs arise primarily from…

choices.label: A
choices.body: CPUs being unable to multiply matrices

choices.label: B
choices.body: Loss functions that only accept two tokens

choices.label: C
choices.body: The tokenizer forbidding sequences longer than 10 tokens

choices.label: D
choices.body: Quadratic attention cost and finite memory for activations or KV cache.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Longer contexts increase memory and compute; architectures and caches must scale accordingly.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Hardware limits exist, but the binding issue is model design and memory.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Cross-entropy applies per token across the whole window.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Modern tokenizers support thousands+ positions with engineering limits.

medium.prompt: For batch inference with KV cache, each sequence in the batch needs…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Separate cache slots (or paged blocks) so prefixes do not overwrite each other.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Recomputation of the full prompt every token for all rows

choices.label: C
choices.body: No storage because batches are stateless

choices.label: D
choices.body: A single shared cache with no sequence id

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Parallel decoding requires isolated K/V history per request in the batch.
